equity_bridge.item: Put and call option liabilities over NCI (Genesis GBP774m, Cosmos, Thailand, other) at PV of exercise price
equity_bridge.note: H1 FY27 balance sheet 1 Aug 2026: current 38 + non-current 801 (FY26: 855; H1 FY26: 1,020). Stands in for the NCI claim; book NCI GBP460m not deducted on top. Cosmos 20% call (~EUR44m) exercised 28 Aug 2026 from cash - neutral to the bridge.

historical_growth.owner_fcf_series_note: Owner FCF (treatment B: reported FCF - lease principal - SBC; IAS 17 years unadjusted): FY16 148.8, FY17 198.2, FY18 165.0, FY19 191.7, FY20 418.8, FY21 648.0 (COVID rent deferrals + working-capital release), FY22 664.1, FY23 334.4, FY24 208.7, FY25 292.0, FY26 443.0. 5yr CAGR is off the inflated FY21 base; 3yr off the depressed FY23.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Management medium-term organic target ('ahead of 2-3% market growth', space growth 2-3% p.a.) - not the historical CAGRs, which are inflated by M&A (Finish Line, Hibbett, Courir, MIG, ISRG; revenue 5yr 15.5%) and by the July-2021 GBP464m placing (equity 5yr 19.3%).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 19.3% diverges >30% from owner-FCF 5yr CAGR -7.3% and from the 2.5% forward rate: book value grew by acquisition and a placing while per-share owner FCF did not compound. Historical rates are not a usable forward proxy.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGR (5yr -7.3%) is far below reported-FCF CAGR (0.5%): lease cash grew from GBP285m (FY21) to GBP657m (FY26) with the acquired US/EU store estates, so an increasing share of reported cash generation is pre-rent. Share count rose 4,866m -> 5,158m with the 2021 placing, then fell to 4,883m diluted on buybacks.

scenario_narratives.base: JD delivers the lowered FY27 guidance (PBTAI GBP700-800m, FCF GBP460-520m) at the trough of the footwear product cycle, then compounds organic revenue at the 2-3% market rate plus disciplined space growth, with adjusted EBITDA margin recovering from ~15% to FY26's ~15.8% as supply-chain and e-commerce investments annualise and the NA estate is rationalised. The GBP200m/yr buyback and progressive dividend absorb the cash. The Genesis minority is bought out in FY30/31 at the option formula, already deducted in the bridge.
scenario_narratives.bull: A NA consumer and 'heat' product recovery from FY28, successful Europe margin build toward high-single-digit operating margin, apparel mix gains and capital-light franchising (Mexico 140+ stores) lift organic growth to 4-4.5% and adjusted EBITDA back to ~17%; the market re-rates a net-cash retailer with a 10%+ FCF yield.
scenario_narratives.bear: Like-for-like decline is structural (brand DTC, allocation, consumer); a lease-heavy fixed-cost estate turns falling sales into margin compression to ~13%, a third guidance cut follows, and board instability slows the response. Cash generation holds but the exit multiple stays single-digit.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on a lease-as-operating-cost basis: every pound of rent (principal and interest, GBP657m in FY26) is charged inside the flows and lease liabilities are kept out of net debt, so the GBP3.1bn IFRS-16 liability is neither ignored nor double-counted. The minorities' claim is taken at the GBP839m put/call liability the Group itself carries, not the GBP460m book NCI. The explicit FY27 year is tied to the reaffirmed FCF guidance; thereafter growth is the 2-3% market, not the M&A-inflated history. Risk is carried in the scenarios and in a 30% bear weight, with one 9.5% GBP WACC across scenarios and a 12x cap on the terminal multiple for a cyclical, structurally slow-growth retailer. SBC is near zero so house and street values coincide.
key_risks_to_valuation: Brand-partner dependency: Nike reportedly >40% of US revenue; allocation or DTC shifts are outside JD's control and hit margin before revenue
Operating leverage on a 4,800-store leased estate: a 1pp fall in sustained EBITDA margin is ~GBP130m of owner FCF, ~25% of the base FCF

Genesis put/call settles FY30/31 on an EBITDA-multiple formula: if JD US outperforms, the GBP774m liability grows (it was GBP993m at H1 FY26) and the bridge deduction is too small; if it underperforms the liability shrinks but so do the flows
FX translation: ~72% of revenue in USD/EUR against GBP reporting; FY26 carried a GBP154m translation loss
Governance: interim chair, reported board split over the CEO, Pentland's ~55% control; a strategy change (M&A resumption, dividend policy) would alter the capital-allocation assumptions

Working-capital drag is modelled as a permanent 0.5pp margin haircut; if inventory discipline delivers the guided improvement the model is ~GBP60m/yr too conservative, if new-store inventory build continues at FY26's pace it is ~GBP150m/yr too generous

data_sources.financials: JD.L_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, GBP millions, FY2016-FY2026 annuals + H1 FY27, 5:1 split restated); JD.L_Annual_FY2026.txt (cash-flow statement p142, free-cash-flow summary p41, adjusting items p39, note 8/15 lease interest, note 33 SBC, auditor's KAM on the Genesis option GBP787m); JD.L_HalfYear_H1-2027.txt (balance sheet 1 Aug 2026, note 8 put/call GBP839m, EPS note diluted 4,883m, FCF reconciliation); JD.L_Quarterly_Q2-2027.txt (guidance cut 20 Aug 2026)
data_sources.qualitative: JD.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-10): business model, bull/bear axes, FY27 guidance, governance events

inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted average diluted, 26 weeks to 1 August 2026 (H1 FY27 note: basic 4,843m + 40m dilutive awards = 4,883m). Held FLAT: SBC (c.GBP5-6m/yr, <0.05% of revenue) is expensed in the flows, so no dilution is compounded. The rolling GBP200m/yr buyback (second FY27 GBP100m tranche running since Aug-2026 at ~85p, c.118m shares) is NOT credited: at ~85p vs a base IV well above that, buying back below IV is accretive, so a flat count is the conservative convention.
inputs.last_fcf_note: last_fcf = reported_fcf 956 (statutory OCF 1,357 - capex 401, FY26; OCF is already after GBP149m lease interest, GBP32m non-lease interest and GBP165m tax) - lease principal 508 - SBC 5 = 443, i.e. company-definition FCF 462 less the GBP11m shareholder-arrangement receipt and the GBP12m 'other non-current assets' line. Interest income (GBP11m) sits in investing, not in OCF, so there is nothing to strip from the base; net cash of GBP168m is <0.4x the FCF base so it is immaterial anyway.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY26 interest received GBP11m is classified in investing activities and is not inside reported_fcf; set to 0 here so last_fcf is not double-adjusted. Net cash (GBP168m ex-leases) is far below 1x the FCF base.
inputs.sbc_source: FY26 Annual Report cash-flow reconciliation note 33 'Share-based payments 5' (FY25: 1); H1 FY27 GBP6m. EquityAwardTaxes nil in all periods. Effectively an SBC-zero filer.
inputs.buyback_note: FY26 financing outflow GBP201m (two GBP100m tranches); H1 FY27 GBP101m (136.8m shares at avg GBP0.73). Company guides a rolling GBP200m annual programme.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in GBP millions; LSE quote in pence (GBp = 1/100 GBP). fx_rate 100 converts model GBP/share to quote pence/share. No dual listing to parity-check; conversion is definitional, not a market rate.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: 31 January (52/53 weeks; FY26 = 52 weeks to 31 January 2026)
inputs.wacc_rationale: GBP-denominated flows discounted at a GBP-built rate: 10y gilt ~4.5% + beta ~1.2 x 5.5% UK ERP = cost of equity ~11%; interest-bearing debt is immaterial ex-leases (net cash GBP168m) and leases are treated as operating cost, so WACC ~ 9.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality, NA consumer, brand-allocation and governance risk are carried in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B) - leases as operating cost. Full lease cash (principal + interest, both on the cash-flow statement: FY26 GBP508m principal in financing + GBP149m interest in operating = GBP657m, 5.2% of revenue; TTM to H1 FY27 GBP712m = 5.6%) is charged inside the flows via lease_cost_pct_path, and lease liabilities (GBP3,104m at 1 Aug 2026) are EXCLUDED from net_debt. D&A for cash-tax EBIT is owned-asset D&A only (FY26 GBP404m of the GBP966m total; GBP562m was right-of-use depreciation), so the lease is not charged twice. Pre-FY2020 (IAS 17) history needs no adjustment; FY2020 onward owner FCF deducts lease principal.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI charged once, in the bridge. Flows are whole-group consolidated. The material minorities (20% of Genesis/JD US; 40% JD Thailand; Cosmos 20%) all sit under put/call options that the Group carries as a liability at the PV of the exercise price: GBP839m at 1 Aug 2026 (current 38 + non-current 801; Genesis alone GBP774m, exercisable FY30/31 on an EBITDA-multiple formula). That liability is deducted in equity_bridge as the NCI claim; the GBP460m book NCI is NOT deducted on top (it is the same economic interest, carried at a lower historical-cost amount). Calibration: engine FY0 NOPAT ~GBP700m vs reported adjusted profit after tax GBP641m less NCI share GBP32m = GBP609m attributable; the gap is non-lease interest (GBP26m post-tax) plus lease principal 508 < ROU depreciation 562 (GBP40m post-tax) - within non-operating noise.
inputs.ebitda_definition: Adjusted EBITDA = operating profit before adjusting items + total D&A (FY26: 1,035 + 966 = 2,001 = 15.8% of revenue; FY25 16.0%; FY24 16.1%; FY23 16.7%; H1 FY27 857/5,899 = 14.5%). Store impairments (GBP119m FY26, GBP112m FY25) are excluded as non-cash because the store capex is already charged in full through capex_pct. The margin PATH is stated NET of a ~0.5pp chronic working-capital drag (inventory for new larger stores, receivables; outflows FY25 -137, FY26 -248, FY27 guidance implies ~-80 on flat revenue) that the engine's growth-linked wc_capture cannot carry on a flat top line. So path 15.3% = ~15.8% adjusted EBITDA margin less 0.5pp.
inputs.guidance_tie: FY27 (Y1) base build: revenue -1.0% (H1 -0.7%, Q2 organic -1.3%, FX translation headwind at GBP/USD 1.34); adjusted EBITDA net of WC drag 14.5%; lease 5.7%; owned D&A 3.2%; capex 3.2% (guided 3.0-3.5%); cash tax 25% (adjusted ETR 24.8%). Gives ~GBP530m unlevered owner FCF, ~GBP505m after GBP25m non-lease net interest, inside the company's reaffirmed FY27 FCF guidance of GBP460-520m and consistent with PBTAI guidance of GBP700-800m (mid GBP750m).
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (Drivers route) with the non-US adaptations: GBP WACC, lease treatment (B), NCI via put/call liability in the bridge, SBC-zero house/street band. Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md: operating company, non-US, cyclical consumer retailer. First valuation of this ticker (no prior DCF, no memory entry). Horizon 10 years: year-1 margin is depressed by the current product cycle and NA consumer weakness and recovers through Y5. Terminal cap 12x owner FCF (cyclical, structurally 2-3% market) vs today's ~9.6x EV/owner-FCF; Gordon at 9.5%/2.0% would be 13.6x so the cap binds in base. House/street band is degenerate: SBC is <0.05% of revenue, so street IV exceeds house IV by only ~3p and band_position is not meaningful - read it as null. Price is the 9-Oct-2026 LSE close; refresh at next close.

bear.narrative: LFL declines (-2.8% H1 FY27) prove structural: Nike/adidas push DTC and cut allocation 'heat', Dick's-owned Foot Locker competes harder in NA, the core 16-24 customer stays squeezed. Revenue falls three years then limps at 1.5%; fixed rents on a 4,800-store leased estate (lease cost rising to 6% of sales) and promotional intensity push margin to ~13% with a third guidance cut; governance (interim chair, CEO dispute) delays the response. Exit multiple capped at 10x.

base.narrative: FY27 at the guided trough (-1% revenue, margin 14.5% net of WC drag), then organic growth at 2-3% market-plus-space, margin recovering to FY26's level by Y5 as the Heerlen/Morgan Hill DCs, e-commerce re-platform and Finish Line/Hibbett rationalisation annualise. No M&A. Lease cost held at the TTM 5.6% of sales; capex at the guided 3.0-3.5% midpoint.

bull.narrative: North American consumer and the footwear 'heat' cycle turn in FY28; space growth plus Mexico/Middle East franchising and apparel mix lift organic growth to 4-4.5%; Europe reaches the targeted high-single-digit operating margin and group adjusted EBITDA returns to the FY23-24 ~17% gross (16.5% net of WC drag); rents lever on rising sales.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% house default to 30%: two consecutive guidance cuts (FY27 PBTAI GBP750-850m -> GBP700-800m), persistent LFL declines (-2.8% H1 FY27, NA -4.5% organic in Q2), >40% of US revenue from one brand partner that is pushing DTC, and a chair who left after failing to remove the CEO. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right together - a NA consumer turn, a new footwear product cycle and Europe margin delivery - and none is in evidence yet. Base 50%: the cash-flow guidance has held through both cuts, net cash ex-leases is GBP168m and buybacks are being funded from FCF, so the trough-then-market-growth path is the central case.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
